title: dedicated-autoscaler-burst-util-reporting-fix: correct rlimit calc and improve metrics
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Fixes incorrect burst rlimit calculation that could artificially throttle tenant burst capacity; improves utilization reporting and adds additional unit/integration tests.
description: Context: We observed in production that dedicated fleet autoscaler was occasionally rejecting legitimate burst requests due to an incorrect application of the per-fleet rlimit when multiple priority buckets were active. This manifested as elevated 429s during short spikes even when aggregate capacity was available. Motivation: Correct burst accounting so that throughput guarantees are honored and utilization metrics reflect real capacity. This PR fixes the rlimit calculation bug, tightens tokenbucket smoothing boundaries, and improves the emitted utilization metrics to include per-priority queue breakdowns for debugging and dashboards. Changes: 1) Fix calculation in autoscaler/token_bucket.go to aggregate available burst tokens across compatible pools before applying per-tenant rlimit. 2) Add smoothing clamp to avoid negative available tokens during high-concurrency drains. 3) Emit new metrics: dedicated.autoscaler.burst_tokens.available_by_priority and dedicated.autoscaler.burst_throttle.count_by_priority. 4) Update fleet-utilization report generator to include priority-level utilization and a 95th percentile peak-burst field. 5) Add unit tests and an integration test that replays a synthetic spike (1000 requests/s for 10s) across two priority classes. 6) Docs: update dedicated autoscaling runbook and console dashboard mapping. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test added and flake-guarded - [x] Metrics validated in local perf lab - [x] Rollout plan in PR description (canary then 100% after 24h) Backwards compatibility: All metric names are additive; config defaults unchanged. Rollout: canary 5% fleet for 6h -> 25% for 12h -> full rollout if no regressions. See linked Linear ENG-4523 for monitoring playbook and rollback steps.

review_comments: Ben Keller (reviewer): The aggregation fix looks correct but please add a unit test for the edge case where pools report slightly negative available due to concurrent drains. Also verify metric cardinality — we don't want an unbounded label set.

Aisha Patel (author): Added a test in token_bucket_test.go that simulates concurrent drains and clamps negative values. Also added a whitelist for priority labels in metrics_registry.yaml to prevent unbounded cardinality.

Sofia Nguyen (reviewer): Confirmed that integration replay in perf lab shows 98% reduction in 429 spike anomalies. Please make sure the rollout plan is documented in the Linear ticket and ops runbook.
Ravi Iyer (approver): LGTM after the minor nits addressed (whitelist and test flake guard). Approving to merge.
